emma_support: Hey team — customer acct-229 hitting repeated 429s despite saying their API key only doing ~20 requests/min. They sent us a curl and response headers. Putting snippets below. Can someone sanity-check scoping?

emma_support: curl they ran:```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-acct229" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 34.200.11.7" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```

emma_support: Response had:```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Scope: org:acct-229
X-Request-ID: rwd-abc123
```

emma_support: Customer insists project-level quota should apply (their project is proj-A with 60rpm), but header shows org scope. They also forwarded a header our proxy adds: `X-Service-Account: svc-ingest-42` (their infra injects it).

luis_sre: Hmm, that suggests our attribution went org-level because service account maps to org binding. Does svc-ingest-42 belong to a different org or is it a cross-project SA?

emma_support: Customer says svc-ingest-42 is a shared service account they run in front of many projects, so requests come from different projects but same SA.

luis_sre: @eng-julian can you check the auth precedence logic? We should prefer API key -> project -> IP -> org, but if a service account header is present we might be mapping to the SA owner org which could override project-scoping.

eng-julian: Looking. Quick note: we intentionally added service-account binding last month so SAs can opt into org-level billing. But might be clobbering project attribution when both API key and SA are present. Need traces for rwd-abc123.

ingest-bot: Indexed logs for rwd-abc123:
``` 
2026-03-12T15:07:21Z request_id=rwd-abc123 auth=api_key:sk-live-acct229 svc_account=svc-ingest-42 nat_ip=34.200.11.7 decision=org_quota_applied scope=org:acct-229 reason=sa_owner_binding
```

luis_sre: That line indicates we found the API key but then applied SA owner binding. Which order does the runtime evaluate?

eng-julian: Current heuristic: if X-Service-Account present -> map to SA owner org, unless a project-scoped API key has explicit project attribute AND api_key.protect_project_binding=true. Looks like this API key is projectless (legacy keys).

maya_pm: Customer expectation: if they pass a project-specific API key it should always be scoped to that project. Legacy keys are confusing. Can we provide immediate workaround for them?

luis_sre: Short-term workaround: they can strip X-Service-Account at their proxy or we can add a tenant header override `X-Redwood-Auth-Force-Project: proj-A` (internal-only, we can honor for troubleshooting).

emma_support: Customer asked if we can flip something on our side — they're not comfortable changing their infra tonight.

eng-julian: I'll do a safe hotfix: change arbitration so explicit API key binding wins over SA owner binding. That should revert behavior to project scope for keys that map to projects. I'll deploy a canary to staging and if green roll to prod for the auth path only. ETA 2–3 hours.

luis_sre: Before deploy, let's add a regression test for mixed-auth (api key + sa header + nat ip) and a metric to track how often SA binding overrides API key.

eng-julian: Agreed. Also adding an emergency config `auth.strict_precedence=true` we can toggle. Planning rollout: canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 3h with monitoring on `rate.scope.switches`.

emma_support: I shared the workaround to the customer (strip header or use tenant override). They said they prefer us to fix. I gave them ETA ~3h. They appreciated the canary approach. :thumbsup:

maya_pm: FYI billing team: this bug could have caused org-level quota consumption for shared SA flows — might affect billing reports. Flagging for review.

luis_sre: Followups: 1) after hotfix, re-evaluate the 14-day backfill attribution for requests that were mis-scoped. 2) Consider warning customers when SA header present and api key projectless.

eng-julian: Will push PR with tests now, link when ready. PR includes note to ops for rollback and the `X-Redwood-Auth-Force-Project` debug header.

emma_support: Thanks all — keeping thread open until prod canary & customer confirmation.

ingest-bot: deploy-canary: auth-service v2026.3.12-canary deployed to stg at 2026-03-12T17:02:00Z

eng-julian: Canary looks stable, metrics: `rate.scope.switches` dropped SA-overrides by 98% on canary. Rolling to 10%.

luis_sre: Noted. I will start the monitoring checklist and set an alert for any spike in 429s from acct-229.

emma_support: Customer confirmed they stopped getting 429s after the change on their test traffic. Will ask them to validate prod tomorrow morning and will follow up here. :white_check_mark:
